Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3-day history of dysuria with mild lower abdominal cramping; small amount of hematuria today; malodorous urine.  
  • No fever, nausea, vomiting, flank/back pain, or urinary frequency reported.  
  • Sexually active with new partner (2 months) ⇒ risk for STI and UTI.
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded (patient denied kidney/bladder/bowel conditions).
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Planned: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily × 3 days (exact drug to be selected by clinician).  
  • OTC sodium bicarbonate taken briefly; not helpful.  
- Allergies: Clindamycin – causes swelling (severity not fully characterized).
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Sexually active; uses condoms consistently.  
  • Never had an STI screen.  
  • Last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor echoed “three weeks ago” – conflict noted).  
  • Denies possibility of pregnancy; clinician advised pregnancy test if concerned.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol: social drinking on weekends.  
  • Tobacco: non-smoker.  
  • Other substances: Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives in a flat with friends near college; undergraduate biology student.  
  • No caring responsibilities mentioned.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not ordered; patient never screened.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable (age 19).
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Prescribe short course of oral antibiotic for simple UTI (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim 1 tab BID for 3 days).  
- Advise increased oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
- Recommend abstaining from sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
- Safety-net advice: return/call if no improvement by end of week or sooner if fever, back pain, or systemic symptoms develop (possible pyelonephritis).  
- Discussed possibility of pregnancy; advised home pregnancy test if any concern.  
- Encourage first-time comprehensive STI screen at appropriate clinic/laboratory.  
- Follow-up appointment: as above if symptoms persist or worsen.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals (BP, pulse), BMI, waist circumference, immunisation review, mental health screening, physical activity/diet assessment, urinalysis, STI screen, cervical screening eligibility discussion, alcohol quantity details.  
● Internal contradictions: LMP stated “couple of weeks ago” vs clinician repeating “three weeks ago.”  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor audio gaps but clinical content understandable.
